ash: Quick heads-up — saw weird mem growth in INT8 canary on longctx workloads. KV pages keep expanding even after idle. Observed accuracy dips on eval-suite_b.

maria: Can you paste perf logs + exact model/variant?

ash: Sure, snippet from canary run:```
model: vicuna-13b-int8
run: canary/2026-03-16
mem_peak: 18.2 GB -> 22.1 GB over 10k tokens
kv_pages: +34% allocated, evicts: 0, paging_reads: 12/s
latency_p95: 230ms -> 270ms
eval_loss_delta: +0.006 on longctx suite
```

jon: that's creepy — evicts 0 means eviction not firing or slot residency threshold too high. Did KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD change in the INT8 kernel?

ash: Not afaik. Kernel selection added an int8 path that prefers 128-slot slabs; profiling shows more fragmentation.

devon: I ran tracer with kv_debug=2 — found many tiny free slots between pages, fragmentation everywhere. Quick repro commands:```
./runtimectl profile --kv-trace --range 0-12000 > kv_trace.log
grep "free_slot_size" kv_trace.log | sort | uniq -c | head
```

ash: excerpt from kv_trace.log: "free_slot_size: 8kb" repeated 1200x, "free_slot_size: 1kb" 7800x. lots of tiny holes.

maria: hypothesis: INT8 kernels change kv slot alignment (8-byte -> 1-byte packed) causing slab packing mismatch with the coalescer. That increases metadata overhead and prevents coalescing across page boundaries.

jon: Also check batching heuristics: int8 path batched more aggressively so KV cache warmups persist and prevent evictions (continuous reuse), but fragmentation prevents reuse. Strange interplay between batching, kernel, and allocator.

perf-bot: Summary metrics for canary/2026-03-16 (vicuna-13b-int8):
- tokens/sec: 820 -> 750 (-8.5%)
- avg mem/case: 18.2GB -> 21.9GB
- p95 latency: 230ms -> 275ms
link: https://perf.redwood/profiles/2179802468

devon: quick mitigations to try on canary:
- lower PREFETCH_WINDOW from 2048 -> 1024
- set KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.65 (was 0.85)
- enable slab_coalesce=true

maria: Good. Can we reproduce with synthetic longctx harness?

ash: yes, repro script:```
./stress_test_longctx --model vicuna-13b-int8 --tokens 15000 --pattern long-dialogue
```

jon: plan: A) rollback int8 kernel allocator flags on canary; B) run slab coalesce patch in canary; C) run quantitative eval comparing BF16 vs INT8 accuracy vs mem.

ash: I'll try coalesce patch now, pushing branch ash/kv-int8-coalesce.

Buildbot: build queued for ash/kv-int8-coalesce
Buildbot: build passed — integration tests OK

perf-bot: After coalesce patch (ash/kv-int8-coalesce) on canary:
- mem_peak: 18.2GB -> 19.3GB
- kv_frag_index: 34% -> 12%
- eval_loss_delta: +0.001
- tokens/sec: 810

maria: that's promising — much of the mem growth tamed and accuracy recovered to near BF16 baseline. We still need kernel-level alignment fix though.

jon: I'll open a ticket for kernel allocator alignment and kernel-selection heuristics: RD-2984. Assigning to eng-runtime.

ash: added logs, kv_trace, and perf links to RD-2984. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
